keyVerseText: And God's anger was kindled because he went: and the angel of the LORD stood in the way for an adversary against him. Now he was riding upon his ass, and his two servants were with him.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun שָׂטָן (sâṭân) derives from the root verb שָׂטַן (sâṭan), which means to act as an adversary or to resist. This root conveys the idea of opposition or standing against someone, often in a personal or national context. The literal sense of 'one who opposes' or 'resists' adds depth beyond the English word 'Satan,' emphasizing the role of an adversary who actively withstands or challenges another party.
usageInScripture: The word שָׂטָן appears 27 times in Scripture, used variously to denote a general adversary or specifically the arch-enemy known as Satan. Its top translations include phrases like 'and Satan,' 'unto Satan,' and 'for an adversary,' reflecting its dual usage as both a human or national opponent and a superhuman adversary. This range shows the term's flexibility in describing opposition, whether earthly or spiritual, highlighting the persistent presence of resistance against God's purposes.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding שָׂטָן as fundamentally an adversary who resists is crucial for grasping the biblical portrayal of spiritual conflict. This word reveals that Satan is not merely a name but a role—one who opposes God's will and the people of God. Recognizing Satan as the ultimate adversary underscores the reality of spiritual warfare and the need for vigilance and faith in Christ, who overcomes all opposition. This insight encourages believers to see their struggles as part of a larger cosmic battle where God remains sovereign.
keyVerseReflection: Numbers 22:22 describes God's anger being kindled because a man proceeded on his journey, and the angel of the LORD stood in the way as an adversary against him. Here, the word שָׂטָן conveys the idea of a divine opposition placed to resist the man's path. This usage highlights that opposition can be ordained by God to fulfill His purposes, reminding us that adversaries, even when challenging, are under God's sovereign control.
